front: First step in building an MCS
back: Make goals explicit: identify the stakeholders that matter to the entity, then their expectations. Performance dimensions are always organisation-specific.
A group or individual liable to affect, or be affected by, the achievement of the entity's objectives.
Many stakeholders; ambiguous or contradictory expectations; relative importance hard to assess and dynamic (depends on type of organisation/entity, institutional context, sector).
The areas that the entity's management seeks to achieve, defined in qualitative terms.
Potential ways of achieving a goal. Actions on cost are only one of them.
Operational translation of a goal (where we want to go) OR a line of action (how we get there) into a result to be achieved.
The goals pursued by an entity and the lines of action chosen to achieve them (including the resources consumed).
A schematic representation of the goals that make sense at a given time, the lines of action chosen, and the cause-and-effect links between them.
A schematic representation of cause-and-effect relationships between aggregates, usually based on a mathematical formalism.
A manager's subjective representation → aim for convergence (vertical & horizontal) and allow change (learning function).
Modelling shapes actors' representations AND behaviour → risk of performative bias, vigilance needed.
Priority action guidelines set by leaders to achieve the goals – resulting from the chosen positioning, the sector's key success factors and cyclical priorities.
Must be consistent with the strategy (key success factors + strategic positioning) and with cyclical priorities.
